chapter_title_en: The Gold Rush of the Daoist Scripture Hall
chapter_seo_title: Desolate Era Ch 270 — The Great Book Heist of the Daoist Scripture Hall
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning and the crew discover a vast Daoist Scripture Hall in the Immortal Estate and scramble for technique books — abridged vs complete editions, Shaoyin Nong’s rage, and the economics of demon slaves.
og_title: Desolate Era Ch 270: The Gold Rush of the Daoist Scripture Hall
og_description: It’s a free-for-all in the Immortal Estate’s library! Ji Ning grabs over a million technique manuals while Shaoyin Nong plots his next move. Xianxia treasure-hunting at its finest.
twitter_description: A gold rush of ancient techniques in the Daoist Scripture Hall — complete, abridged, and everything in between. Also, Shaoyin Nong is very, very angry.

lore_anchors.definition: The central library of a sect or clan, housing the complete collection of its techniques, secret arts, and divine abilities. Often divided into abridged public sections and secret, heavily guarded chambers for full editions.

A partial copy of a cultivation technique, typically showing only the first few pages or sections. Used in public halls to prevent full secrets from being stolen, while the complete edition is kept in a hidden chamber.
A full, uncut version of a technique or manual, containing the entire path from start to finish. Extremely valuable when rare, and a major haul for any growing clan.
A unique treasure that allows its bearer to sense and refine the core nexus of an Immortal estate, gradually gaining total control over its formations and secrets.
The heart of a major structure’s formation network. Once refined by a cultivator, it grants total control over all sub-formations, enabling detection of hidden rooms and treasures.
A type of aquatic demon that can be trained and equipped as a Dao-soldier. Their armor is valuable as a military asset, especially in sea-based territories.
The original owner of the Immortal estate. A powerful Celestial Immortal who carved out his own domain; his treasure hall and scripture hall are the main draw for the exploration party.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn’t Xue Hongyi’s plan work?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Shaoyin Nong wants to enslave the demon Dao-soldiers, not set them free. Letting them go is throwing away a fortune worth more than the treasures he spent to get in. It’s pure Xianxia economics — slaves are more valuable than treaties.

Abridged manuals show only the first section of a technique. They’re used in public scripture halls to prevent theft of the complete method while still letting disciples browse and choose. Full copies are hidden in secret chambers.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What did Ji Ning actually gain here?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Ji Ning collected hundreds of thousands of Human-ranked and Earth-ranked techniques. For his tribe, the Ji Clan, this is a massive upgrade — enough to train generations of Xiantian and Zifu cultivators without buying from the market.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Shaoyin Nong taking so long to refine the hall’s nexus?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Refining a central nexus is a slow process, requiring the cultivator to sit and channel their energy into the core for an extended period. The more powerful the structure, the longer the refinement takes. An hour is actually quite fast.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Are there any top-tier techniques hidden in the hall?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Shaoyin Nong believes the best techniques are hidden elsewhere. But with an hour of nexus refinement, he’ll be able to detect everything in the hall — so the race is on to find them before his control is total.
